newsitem.title: USA: World Bank loans rose to record $20 bln in 96-97.
newsitem.headline: World Bank loans rose to record $20 bln in 96-97.

text.p: The World Bank lent its member states a record $20 billion in the year to the end of June, and China and Russia topped the list of borrowers, the bank said on Tuesday.

A World Bank statement said disbursements from the Bank and the International Development Association, which makes low-interest loans to the world's poorest countries, were some $700 million higher than last year's $19.3 billion.
"I am very encouraged by the fact that the level of our disbursements...rose four percent from last year," said Gautam Kaji, World Bank managing director for operations.
"This coincides with an improvement in the quality of our project portfolio. We are disbursing more for better projects."
The World Bank figures showed that China, which took $2.82 billion of funds, was by far the largest single borrower from the bank, followed by Russia with $1.72 billion.
The Russia loans included $800 million for social reform, the largest ever loan for the region and the third biggest credit in the World Bank's 52-year history.
Other big borrowers included India, which took $1.53 billion, Argentina, with $1.48 billion and Brazil with 993 million.
The World Bank and IDA target most of their loans at specific sectors in a country's economy, although IDA also provides balance of payments support for some poor countries.
